about: Detection cut-offs and Safety bounds for Spec 3 (backend/detection.py load_content). Proposed by the AI / detection lead on 2026-11-15 for the integration lead to approve. Sources checked; see docs/cut-offs-needed.md. Tuned on the four PMData crew replays (ticket 13). Reviewed by the integration lead on 2026-11-15 (Spec 5 ticket 05): linted, AHA links added, body_temperature bound added; glucose bound set to ADA level 2 (54-250 mg/dL) on top of the personal baseline. Still needs qualified medical review.

cutoffs.name: cusum_k
cutoffs.label: team value
cutoffs.source: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook 6.3.2.3 (k = half the shift to detect): https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/pmc/section3/pmc323.htm

cutoffs.name: acute_amber
cutoffs.label: team value
cutoffs.source: 3-sigma limits (NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook 6.3.2) raised to 4 after tuning on crew replays: 3 gave 0.14 alerts per crew-day, 4 gave 0.11

cutoffs.name: min_anchor_sd
cutoffs.label: team value
cutoffs.source: Tuned on crew replays: a 14-day Anchor gives about 1 bpm spread, too tight for months of real data

cutoffs.name: hr_high
cutoffs.label: Earth reference, no space data
cutoffs.source: AHA 2025 Adult Tachyarrhythmia With a Pulse Algorithm: heart rate typically >=150/min if tachyarrhythmia. https://cpr.heart.org/en/resuscitation-science/cpr-and-ecc-guidelines/algorithms

cutoffs.name: hr_low
cutoffs.label: Earth reference, no space data
cutoffs.source: AHA 2025 Adult Bradycardia With a Pulse Algorithm: heart rate typically less than 50 per minute if bradyarrhythmia. https://cpr.heart.org/en/resuscitation-science/cpr-and-ecc-guidelines/algorithms

cutoffs.name: sbp_low
cutoffs.label: Earth reference, no space data
cutoffs.source: AHA 2020 Part 3 (Panchal et al.): systolic 90 mmHg is a common hypotension cutoff; definitions vary. https://www.ahajournals.org/doi/10.1161/CIR.0000000000000916

cutoffs.name: expected_shift
cutoffs.label: astronaut study, group average, not a limit
cutoffs.source: Stahn AC et al. Increased core body temperature in astronauts during long-duration space missions. Sci Rep 2017;7:16180: resting core body temperature rose about 1 °C, developing over 2.5 months. Other indicators: no in-flight source, none applied. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5701078/

cutoffs.name: return_to_gravity_shift
cutoffs.label: group averages after landing, not limits
cutoffs.source: NASA Apollo AP005, Table 6, first postflight minus preflight (61.6->69.7, 76.4->99.8, 118.8->105.8): https://nlsp.nasa.gov/search/data/details/e1fa5c55-ddfe-5548-91ba-864080319f44?dataType=EXPERIMENTS

safety_bounds.label: Earth reference, no space data
safety_bounds.source: AHA 2025 Adult Bradycardia and Tachyarrhythmia With a Pulse Algorithms: https://cpr.heart.org/en/resuscitation-science/cpr-and-ecc-guidelines/algorithms. Not used for resting_heart_rate: AHA notes a low rate can be normal in athletes, and one crew's normal is 49 bpm.

safety_bounds.label: Earth reference, no space data
safety_bounds.source: AHA 2020 Part 3 (Panchal et al.): systolic 90 mmHg is a common hypotension cutoff. No upper limit sourced. https://www.ahajournals.org/doi/10.1161/CIR.0000000000000916

safety_bounds.label: Earth reference, no space data
safety_bounds.source: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes 2025, Section 6, Table 6.2 (CGM metrics): TBR <54 mg/dL is level 2 hypoglycemia; TAR >250 mg/dL is level 2 hyperglycemia. Diabetes-care limits, used with the personal baseline. Real astronaut data: 3 of 28 Inspiration4 values (NASA OSDR OSD-575) are below 54 mg/dL, all at R+45. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11635034/ https://osdr.nasa.gov/bio/repo/data/studies/OSD-575

safety_bounds.label: low: NASA-STD-3001 (space standard); high: Earth reference, no space data
safety_bounds.source: Low: NASA-STD-3001 Volume 1 Rev C, Definitions: hypothermia occurs as body temperature falls below 95 °F (35 °C). https://standards.nasa.gov/sites/default/files/standards/NASA/C//nasa-std-3001-vol-1-rev-c-signature.pdf High: CDC ill-traveler definitions (Fever): a measured temperature of 100.4 °F [38 °C] or greater. https://www.cdc.gov/quarantine/maritime/definitions-signs-symptoms-conditions-ill-travelers.html Caution: resting core temperature rose about 1 °C over 2.5 months of long-duration flight (Stahn 2017), so 38 °C may be reached by healthy crew in flight; see expected_shift. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5701078/
